create_or_update_file.rationale: `Create or update a single file in a GitHub repository` can write agent-supplied `content` and `message` into an agent-chosen repository/path/branch; a public GitHub repository is attacker-readable.

search_repositories.rationale: `Search for GitHub repositories` returns repository data; public repository names/descriptions are attacker-authored, so UNTRUSTED. The description does not say results are public-only; authenticated GitHub search may include private repositories reachable with the user's credentials, so SECRET is kept as undetermined.

create_repository.rationale: `Create a new GitHub repository in your account` can create a repository with agent-supplied `name` and `description`; because `private` controls privacy, a non-private repository can be publicly attacker-readable.

get_file_contents.rationale: `Get the contents of a file or directory from a GitHub repository` returns file contents. Public or multi-writer repository contents can be attacker-authored, so UNTRUSTED. The description does not limit access to public repositories, so private repository contents reachable with the user's credentials may be returned; SECRET is kept as undetermined.

push_files.rationale: `Push multiple files to a GitHub repository in a single commit` writes agent-supplied file `content`, paths, and `message` into an agent-chosen repository/branch; if the repository is public this is attacker-readable.

create_issue.rationale: `Create a new issue in a GitHub repository` writes agent-supplied `title` and `body` to an issue in an agent-chosen repository; public issues are attacker-readable.

create_pull_request.rationale: `Create a new pull request in a GitHub repository` writes agent-supplied `title` and `body/description` and exposes chosen branches in a repository; public pull requests are attacker-readable.

fork_repository.rationale: `Fork a GitHub repository to your account or specified organization` changes public GitHub-visible repository state. It is not explicit whether the fork will be private or what data is returned/published beyond the chosen source/organization, so SINK is kept under the least-restrictive reading.

create_branch.rationale: `Create a new branch in a GitHub repository` writes an agent-supplied `branch` name into an agent-chosen repository; branch names in public repositories are attacker-readable.

list_commits.rationale: `Get list of commits of a branch in a GitHub repository` returns commit data. Public or multi-writer commit messages/authors can be attacker-authored, so UNTRUSTED. The description does not restrict to public repositories, so private repository commit data may be returned with the user's credentials; SECRET is kept as undetermined.

list_issues.rationale: `List issues in a GitHub repository with filtering options` returns issue titles/bodies/comments metadata that public users can author, so UNTRUSTED. The description does not limit to public repositories, so issues in private repositories reachable with the user's credentials may be returned; SECRET is kept as undetermined.

update_issue.rationale: `Update an existing issue in a GitHub repository` writes agent-supplied `title`, `body`, labels/state, and assignments to an agent-chosen issue; public issues are attacker-readable.

add_issue_comment.rationale: `Add a comment to an existing issue` writes agent-supplied `body` to an agent-chosen issue; public issue comments are attacker-readable.

search_code.rationale: `Search for code across GitHub repositories` returns code snippets/metadata. Public repository code can be attacker-authored, so UNTRUSTED. The description does not say public-only, so private code reachable with the user's credentials may be returned; SECRET is kept as undetermined.

search_issues.rationale: `Search for issues and pull requests across GitHub repositories` returns issue/PR text that public users can author, so UNTRUSTED. The description does not say public-only, so private issues or pull requests reachable with the user's credentials may be returned; SECRET is kept as undetermined.

search_users.rationale: `Search for users on GitHub` returns user data; GitHub usernames/profile text can be chosen by outside users, so the returned content is UNTRUSTED.

get_issue.rationale: `Get details of a specific issue in a GitHub repository` returns issue details such as title/body/comments that outside users can author, so UNTRUSTED. The description does not restrict to public repositories, so private issue details reachable with the user's credentials may be returned; SECRET is kept as undetermined.

get_pull_request.rationale: `Get details of a specific pull request` returns PR details such as title/body/branch data that outside contributors can author, so UNTRUSTED. The description does not restrict to public repositories, so private PR details reachable with the user's credentials may be returned; SECRET is kept as undetermined.

list_pull_requests.rationale: `List and filter repository pull requests` returns PR data from a repository; public contributors can author PR titles/bodies/branch names, so UNTRUSTED. The description does not restrict to public repositories, so private PR data reachable with the user's credentials may be returned; SECRET is kept as undetermined.

create_pull_request_review.rationale: `Create a review on a pull request` posts agent-supplied review `body` and review `comments` to an agent-chosen pull request; public PR reviews/comments are attacker-readable.

merge_pull_request.rationale: `Merge a pull request` changes repository state and can write agent-supplied `commit_title` and `commit_message` into the merge commit; public repository commits are attacker-readable.

get_pull_request_files.rationale: `Get the list of files changed in a pull request` returns file names/patch information that PR authors can control, so UNTRUSTED. The description does not restrict to public repositories, so private PR file changes reachable with the user's credentials may be returned; SECRET is kept as undetermined.

get_pull_request_status.rationale: `Get the combined status of all status checks for a pull request` returns status-check data. Status/check names, descriptions, or URLs may be authored by integrations or multi-writer repository actors, so UNTRUSTED is kept. The description does not restrict to public repositories, so private PR status data reachable with the user's credentials may be returned; SECRET is kept as undetermined.

update_pull_request_branch.rationale: `Update a pull request branch with the latest changes from the base branch` writes to an agent-chosen PR branch in a GitHub repository. The description does not state whether the repository/PR is private or public, nor whether only non-content state changes occur, so SINK is kept under the least-restrictive reading for public repository writes.

get_pull_request_comments.rationale: `Get the review comments on a pull request` returns review comments authored by outside contributors, so UNTRUSTED. The description does not restrict to public repositories, so private PR comments reachable with the user's credentials may be returned; SECRET is kept as undetermined.

get_pull_request_reviews.rationale: `Get the reviews on a pull request` returns review bodies/comments that outside contributors can author, so UNTRUSTED. The description does not restrict to public repositories, so private PR reviews reachable with the user's credentials may be returned; SECRET is kept as undetermined.

value_conditions.effect: Creates the repository as private; this can remove the public-repository attacker-readable SINK aspect for create_repository, assuming no attacker has access to the user's private account data.

notes: No output schemas were advertised, so identifier_output_fields and attacker_named_fields are left empty unless the entire returned value was clearly untrusted text; injectable_output_fields uses "return" for read tools whose returned GitHub content can include outside-authored text.
No advertised tool description says the tool is off by default, so default_enabled is true for all tools.
